newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia cracks down on Kalimantan rioters.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia cracks down on Kalimantan rioters.

text.p: Indonesia's military said on Thursday it was cracking down on rioters in the country's West Kalimantan province on Borneo island after the death of a number of people in race riots since late December.

"Sometimes people take it for granted when the armed forces say they plan to take stern action...but this time we will and have taken stern action in West Kalimantan against rioters," an armed forces spokesman told Reuters by telephone.
"We will take action regardless of the people's ethnicity or religion," he added.
The spokesman said a number of people had been killed during riots between the native Dayaks and Moslem migrants from Madura island off eastern Java.
"There have been fatalities, but we are still collecting information from the local military offices before announcing the official figure," he said.
He declined to give further details.
The local military and residents in the province say at least 12 people have died over the past six weeks. Some residents and church sources say the figure could be much higher.

Trouble erupted in West Kalimantan, which borders Malaysia's Sarawak state, in late December following what police said was a fight between Dayak and Maduran youths over a girl at a concert in Sanggau Ledo, about 95 km (60 miles) north of the provincial capital of Pontianak.

The riots later spread to other parts of the province. In Sanggau, 140 km (90 miles) east of Pontianak, Maduran families were still taking refuge in army camps in the area after a series of fights between the two groups.
Malaysia on Wednesday reopened one of 12 border posts between West Kalimantan and Sarawak that Kuala Lumpur had closed following the riots, the Bernama news agency reported.

In Pontianak, residents said the town was quiet. The authorities have imposed a curfew from 11 p.m. to 5 a.m. in the coastal town, while residents in other areas were being confined to their homes after 9 p.m.
Indonesia's official Antara news agency said local religious leaders had issued a statement saying they regretted the disturbances, which they said were not religious in nature.
The Dayaks are often Christian, while the Maduran migrants are Moslem in mostly Islamic Indonesia, where at least 19 people have died since October in a number of religious and ethnic riots.
Tambang Timah has said it was holding talks with Hasan over an equity participation in Busang.
